intro: A diffusion schedule specifies how much signal is retained after repeated noise additions. Per-step retention and cumulative retention answer different questions.
task: Build a linear sequence of beta values and the cumulative product of their complementary alpha values. Interpret the result as a schedule, without simulating a trained denoiser.
requirements: steps is an integer in [2,10000], excluding booleans. Require 0<beta_start<=beta_end<1.
Use steps equally spaced beta values including both endpoints. alpha[t]=1-beta[t], and alpha_bar[t] is the product of alpha[0] through alpha[t], inclusive.
Return a dictionary with betas and alpha_bar arrays of length steps. Index zero already includes the first noise step. Float64 underflow to zero in a long schedule is allowed.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Separate a step from its history
hints.body: The current alpha is one minus beta. The cumulative value multiplies all previous alphas too.

hints.title: Check a constant schedule
hints.body: If beta is constant b, the retained signal at index t is (1-b)**(t+1).

explanation: In the usual forward-noising parameterization, sqrt(alpha_bar) scales the original signal and sqrt(1-alpha_bar) scales independent unit-variance noise. These squared coefficients add to one.
Changing the number of steps while keeping beta endpoints fixed changes cumulative retention. The schedule itself is not a claim about image quality or a trained generation system.

Adapted only the upstream linear-beta branch, with configurable endpoints and both per-step betas and cumulative retention returned. Cosine and sigmoid variants are deliberately outside this contract.
